title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented UCI rituals, recurring campus celebrations, and Anteater symbols.

cards.title: Answer the Anteater war cry
cards.subtitle: UCI school-spirit tradition
cards.notes: Listen for “Zot!” at an Anteater event, then use the three-part call with the crowd rather than treating it as a generic mascot slogan.
cards.short_summary: UCI adopted the anteater’s “Zot!” sound as its rallying cry in October 1965.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Athletics identifies “Zot” as a war cry borrowed from the anteater in the B.C. comic strip and says the student campaign established it before the 1965 mascot election.
cards.access_notes: Use at public UCI spirit or athletics events; confirm each event’s entry policy separately.

cards.title: Learn the Rip ’Em Eaters hand sign
cards.subtitle: UCI Anteater gesture
cards.notes: Check the official illustration and try the hand sign at a game or campus gathering as a simple, no-equipment way to show Anteater affiliation.
cards.short_summary: The hand sign draws on an anteater’s defensive posture and is presented by UCI Athletics as a shared Anteater symbol.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Athletics says the Rip ’Em Eaters hand sign is based on an anteater’s defensive action and was established to give UCI students and alumni a shared sign of pride and camaraderie.
cards.access_notes: Appropriate for public campus and athletics settings.

cards.title: Trace the choice of the Anteater
cards.subtitle: UCI’s mascot tradition
cards.notes: Read the official election account before spotting Peter the Anteater at a public campus event; it explains why this mascot is central to UCI identity.
cards.short_summary: Students selected the Anteater in UCI’s 1965 mascot election.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Athletics reports that student-athletes and a fellow student organized the anteater campaign before the November 30, 1965 student election, in which the Anteater received 55.9 percent of the vote.
cards.access_notes: Mascot appearances vary by event; check the host event’s details.

cards.title: Join the Community Roots Festival
cards.subtitle: Formerly the Rainbow Festival
cards.notes: Use the Cross-Cultural Center schedule to find performances and organization booths, then take time to learn directly from participating campus communities.
cards.short_summary: Founded in 1984, this fall gathering continues the Cross-Cultural Center’s Rainbow Festival tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: The UCI Cross-Cultural Center describes Community Roots Festival, formerly Rainbow Festival, as a longstanding tradition founded in 1984 with cultural performances, interactive booths and student-organization fundraising.
cards.source_title: Community Roots Festival | UC Irvine Cross-Cultural Center
cards.access_notes: See the Cross-Cultural Center page for the current year’s program and participation details.

cards.title: Remember Midnight Magic
cards.subtitle: Historic UCI basketball-season kickoff
cards.notes: Use the UCI archive to understand this basketball kickoff, then check current Athletics and student-event calendars before expecting a present-day edition.
cards.short_summary: UCI’s basketball-season celebration debuted as Midnight Magic in 1998 after earlier Anteater Basketball Bash events.
cards.evidence_claim: A UCI News traditions account states that Midnight Magic debuted in 1998 and became a yearly basketball-season celebration, typically featuring team introductions, scrimmages and skills contests.
cards.source_title: UCI traditions tutorial | UC Irvine News
cards.access_notes: Historical documentation; confirm whether a current edition is scheduled before visiting.

cards.title: Start with SPOP
cards.subtitle: Historic incoming-student orientation tradition
cards.notes: If you are an incoming student or supporter, use UCI’s current orientation information for eligibility and registration rather than relying on this historic format.
cards.short_summary: SPOP was documented by UCI as a summer orientation series introducing incoming students and parents to campus life.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI News described SPOP as a longstanding summer orientation tradition in which incoming freshmen and parents learned about college life and students enrolled in classes.
cards.source_title: UCI traditions tutorial | UC Irvine News
cards.access_notes: Historical account; current orientation formats and registration may differ.

cards.title: Come back for UCI Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Anteater reunion and campus celebration
cards.notes: Follow the Student Alumni Association’s Homecoming information for the current program, and choose the family-friendly daytime activities that fit your visit.
cards.short_summary: The Student Alumni Association calls UCI Homecoming a long-standing tradition that brings Anteaters together for festivities.
cards.evidence_claim: The UCI Student Alumni Association lists UCI Homecoming among its annual events and describes it as a long-standing tradition bringing Anteaters together for festivities in the park.
cards.source_title: Student Alumni Association | UCI Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: Consult the current Homecoming schedule and registration information before attending.

cards.title: Make MLK Day a day on
cards.subtitle: Anteater community-service tradition
cards.notes: Register through UCI Volunteer Programs when a service project is posted, and plan to take part in the reflection and community-service components together.
cards.short_summary: UCI Volunteer Programs frames MLK Jr. Day of Service as an Anteater tradition of community service.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Volunteer Programs states that MLK Jr. Day of Service is a tradition for Anteaters to continue Martin Luther King Jr.’s legacy through community service.
cards.source_title: Martin Luther King Jr. Day of Service | UCI Volunteer Programs
cards.access_notes: The official page includes Winter 2026 information; registration and project availability can change.

cards.title: Celebrate campus organizations
cards.subtitle: Annual UCI recognition ceremony
cards.notes: Review the nominees and ceremony details, then attend or support an eligible registered organization during the awards season if participation is open.
cards.short_summary: The Anteater Awards is an annual ceremony recognizing UCI registered campus organizations and volunteer programs.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Campus Organizations calls the Anteater Awards an annual tradition recognizing achievements and contributions of its 600-plus registered campus organizations through a nominations-based ceremony.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists the 2026 ceremony for May 27; verify event access or RSVP requirements.

cards.title: Notice the anteater-nose mace
cards.subtitle: UCI commencement ceremonial tradition
cards.notes: At commencement, look for the mace at the front of the processional and read its official history before the ceremony begins.
cards.short_summary: A California-oak mace shaped like an anteater’s nose leads UCI commencement processions.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI’s commencement-program history states that the UCI Mace was first carried in 2000, is fashioned to resemble an anteater’s nose, and is carried by a distinguished alumnus or alumna to lead the commencement processional.
cards.source_title: Commencement Program 2020 | UCI Paul Merage School of Business
cards.access_notes: Ceremonial viewing is limited to commencement attendees and guests under current event rules.
